finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint checks the host with endswith('example.com'). The check has no leading dot, so ALLOWED_SUFFIX is unused and any domain ending in 'example.com' passes, for example 'evilexample.com' or 'attacker-example.com'. An attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at an internal or metadata IP (169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.x). The server then fetches that address. The response only returns the body length, so the SSRF is semi-blind, but it still allows internal port and service probing and body-length oracles. The hostname is validated at check time and re-resolved at fetch time, so DNS rebinding also works. There is no IP or scheme check; http:// is accepted.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the endswith('example.com') host check, which is bypassable with notexample.com or evilexample.com. No scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP or private-range blocking, and no DNS pinning. httpx does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass does not apply. There is no authentication middleware. The /ping handler (line 23) uses a constant URL and is not a finding.
